Here's a history lesson. It used to be that the accuracy and longevity of a watch was correlated to it's cost. This is partially because more accurate machining costs more money, but it is also because actual precious stones were used within the movements. Bearings made of rubies and sapphires allowed for a very hard surface that would not degrade over time (prolonging accuracy) and they are also low friction. The more of them you had, the higher the watch price, but the better the watch worked. But that was back when people wore mechanical watches. Now a typical digital watch is far more accurate than any of those precision jewelled movements.
